analysis.title: Copper Dashboard: Physical tightness persists with 90% of visible inventories in the US, ongoing supply disruptions, but sentiment weakens
key_insights: Copper has been range-bound for three months at ~$14,000-14,800/t ($6.35-6.70/lb). Sentiment has shifted to 'cautious uncertainty' on US tariff threats and fears of slower AI capex, while global and US PMIs stay strong at 52.6 and 54.9.

Global visible copper inventories rose to 1.1Mt from 975kt in mid-August as US-located stocks keep climbing. About 90% of inventory is now in the US. SHFE plus China bonded inventories are down to 60kt versus over 400kt in late March.
US inventory accumulation has tightened the rest of the world (RoW). Weak mine output, particularly in Chile, adds to this, and China cathode premia have spiked.
Global mined copper production is down 1.3% YTD through August. Chile mined production was down 15% YoY in September. Global apparent demand is down about 2% YTD.
High-frequency indicators are mixed. China cathode premia are up sharply and TC/RCs remain deeply negative, while LME cancelled warrants have fallen since August.
LME speculative positioning has fallen materially and forward pricing is below spot through next year (backwardation).

The Global Copper Supply Tracker covers 25 companies, over 100 mines and 27 countries, about 54% of world supply. September-quarter output fell 1.3% (43kt) and was about 180kt below the June 2025 quarter high. JPM expects a rebound of about 150kt in the December 2026 quarter as Chile recovers from rain impacts.

Covered output is forecast to fall 261kt in 2026, then grow 987kt in 2027 and 1,089kt in 2028. Grasberg and Collahuasi are the largest 2027 contributors, and Cobre Panama drives 2028 assuming a mid-2027 restart.
Greg Shearer's global supply/demand model shows mine growth of 1.43Mt in 2027 and 1.57Mt in 2028, with a modest surplus in coming years. Copper price risk is linked to tariff outcomes.

Metals strategy sees acute physical tightness in China against weaker investor sentiment over US data-centre investment and copper tariffs. Smelter maintenance, constrained scrap and low Chinese social inventories lifted premiums, but technicals have weakened. A sustained break below about $13,850/t could expose further downside.
A prolonged absence of US tariff follow-through is the bigger medium-term risk. Copper redirected away from the US could ease China's shortage and erode price support.

US project pipeline is about 1.3Mtpa, third-largest globally, but most capacity arrives after 2030 with above-average capital intensity. Water access and limited domestic smelting are constraints, and the US is expected to keep a refined deficit of around 1Mt through the decade.

The US carry trade (buy physical, ship to the US, sell COMEX forward) drove the inventory build. With the COMEX premium to LME now largely eliminated, new inflows should slow. Destocking would need a sustained LME premium to COMEX or stronger physical premiums in China and Europe.
Data-center copper demand is modelled at 30t/MW with 25/30/35/40GW of annual capacity growth in 2027-2030. Hyperscaler capex is flagged as a potentially material long-term demand driver.
Ratings: Overweight on CSC, BHP (Australia listing), RIO (Australia listing), GLC, SFR in Australia, FCX in the US, and Antofagasta in EMEA. Underweight on Lundin Mining.
China refined copper net imports are down 12% YTD through August and RoW refined demand is down 15%. China refined demand is up 1% YTD through August.

earnings_insights: JPM 2027 NPAT estimates versus consensus: Glencore US$6,624m vs US$7,668m (-14%), First Quantum US$941m vs US$1,613m (-42%), Lundin Mining US$1,003m vs US$1,326m (-24%), Capstone Copper US$804m vs US$692m (+16%), Freeport US$6,560m vs US$6,041m (+9%). These are estimates, not reported figures.

JPM 2028 NPAT estimates versus consensus: South32 US$508m vs US$1,000m (-49%), Vale BRL 31,353m vs BRL 40,582m (-23%), Capstone Copper US$929m vs US$772m (+20%), Antofagasta US$2,690m vs US$2,341m (+15%), Teck CAD 3,820m vs CAD 2,289m (+67%). These are estimates, not reported figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Manufacturing activity is holding up despite fears of slowing AI capex, which supports copper demand.
US PMI is strong and not reflecting the weaker AI-trade sentiment.
China's official PMI is below 50 in October, down from 50.1 in September.
Range-bound trading with a $13,850/t technical support level flagged.
Weak supply, especially Chile, adds to physical tightness.
Apparent demand is weaker, partly offsetting supply tightness.
Supply growth produces a modest surplus over the coming years.

risk_factors: A sustained break below about $13,850/t could expose copper to further downside.
A prolonged absence of US tariff follow-through could let copper redirected away from the US ease China's shortage and erode price support.
Fears of slower AI and data-center capex could weaken the demand outlook.
Mine supply recovery (Grasberg, Collahuasi, Kamoa-Kakula, Cobre Panama restart) could move the market to a modest surplus.
COMEX inventory could unwind if offshore returns exceed the US carry.
vol_and_positioning: LME net speculative positioning has fallen materially.
Forward pricing is below spot through next year (backwardation).
Smelter treatment charges (TC/RCs) remain deeply negative, indicating a tight concentrate market.
Technical indicators have weakened, with a sustained break below about $13,850/t flagged as a downside risk.
geopolitical: US copper tariff threat and uncertainty over follow-through is the main medium-term price risk.
US critical-minerals security focus is driving US copper project investment.

tension_points.bull_case: Physical tightness persists: 90% of visible inventory sits in the US, China cathode premia have spiked, TC/RCs are deeply negative, Chile output is down 15% YoY and PMIs are strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Speculative positioning has fallen, technicals have weakened, AI capex fears persist, and a lack of US tariff follow-through could release metal and ease China's shortage. Supply is set to grow 1.43Mt in 2027, producing a modest surplus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained break below approximately $13,850/mt on LME copper.
